items.title: [Bug] AMF crashes on an uninitialized NGAP message type while building Error Indication
AMF: Uplink NAS Transport with a mismatched AMF-UE-NGAP-ID terminates the AMF
items.body:
## Affected commit

```
b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7
```

`develop` head of 2026-09-16, carried by the tested image as
`org.opencontainers.image.revision = commit:b2f19d1a`
(`oaisoftwarealliance/oai-amf@sha256:5a4555ac8bee0a69626ca08d91ad4850150e3439771e0d549dc8130fb0942337`,
built 2026-09-17), with `src/common-src` pinned at `c0dcc9aa70da170b3dcd690a34e704be4199f3fd`.

## Problem

An NGAP peer that can reach N2 terminates the AMF with three messages and no authentication: an NG Setup, an
Initial UE Message, and one Uplink NAS Transport whose `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` does not match the one the AMF
allocated for that `RAN-UE-NGAP-ID`. Whatever the AMF sends back after the Initial UE Message is read and
discarded, and nothing is ever sent in answer to it, so no security context ever exists.

While the AMF is down, registration, service request and all N1/N2 signalling for the served area fail.

**Expected behavior.** An inconsistent `AMF-UE-NGAP-ID` is answered with an NGAP Error Indication, cause
`inconsistent-remote-UE-NGAP-ID`, which is what the code intends to do.

**Observed behavior.** The process terminates. 3 rounds of 3, each against an AMF restarted immediately
before the round: `exited exit=139`, `OOMKilled` false, and a safe SBI read answering `400` before the
sequence and nothing after it.

**Cause.** That Error Indication carries a 5GS TMSI the UE NGAP context never sets, and encoding it converts
an empty string with an unguarded `std::stol`:

| step | where |
|---|---|
| mismatch branch | `src/amf-app/amf_n2.cpp:923` |
| builds the 5GS TMSI from `unc->s_tmsi` | `src/amf-app/amf_n2.cpp:938` |
| `std::string s_tmsi;`, declared, default-initialised, never assigned anywhere in the source | `src/contexts/ue_ngap_context.hpp:84` |
| calls `encode()` inline | `ngap/ngap_msgs/ErrorIndication.cpp:169` |
| `(uint32_t) std::stol(m_TmsiValue)`, no `try`/`catch` | `ngap/ngap_ies/FiveGSTmsi.cpp:47` |

`std::stol("")` throws `std::invalid_argument` whose `what()` is `stol`, which is the string the AMF logs.
Nothing catches it, so it reaches `std::terminate()`.

Additionaly:

* The same mismatch check at `amf_n2.cpp:334` (Paging) and `:1819` (Handover Required) logs and returns.
  Line 923 is the only one that builds an Error Indication, and `:942` is the only call to
  `send_ng_error_indication` in the file, which is why only this branch is fatal.
* `amf_n2.cpp:361` pages with the same unset `s_tmsi` through `PagingMsg::setUePagingIdentity` into the same
  `FiveGSTmsi::encode`, so the crash may also be reachable with no attacker involved. That one is a source
  reading and was NOT tested.

## Affected functionality and file paths

NGAP Uplink NAS Transport handling and NGAP Error Indication encoding, in the files listed above.
`FiveGSTmsi.cpp:47` is the only one of the five `std::stol` calls across the two repositories that is not
wrapped in `try`/`catch`.

## Reproduction information

Withheld from this issue, as OAI `SECURITY.md` requires: "do not mention how to reproduce the problem in the
issue description. 

## AI tool disclosure

```
Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5
```

Reached by an AI-driven NGAP/NAS testing workflow; the mechanism above by an AI-assisted source trace that
was then checked against the running process. All of it was reviewed before submission.

## Logs

The AMF's own last lines, one round:

```
[amf_n2] [info]  Received Uplink NAS Transport message, handling
[amf_n2] [debug] Handle Uplink NAS Transport...
[amf_n2] [error] The requested UE (amf_ue_ngap_id: 30583) is not valid, existed UE which's
                 amf_ue_ngap_id (1); aborting Uplink NAS Transport
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
  what():  stol
```

The host kernel, same moment, same process:

```
traps: oai_amf[81487] general protection fault ip:7efd1b0be9a2 sp:7efd13ffe240 error:0
       in libc.so.6[289a2,7efd1b0be000+189000]
```

* Offset `0x289a2` in that libc is `abort+386`, resolved against the libc taken from the AMF image.
* The offset was identical in all three rounds.
* So `abort()`, called by `std::terminate()`, faults, which is why the container reports 139 rather than the
  134 a clean abort would give.

## Proposed patch

```c++
// ngap/ngap_ies/FiveGSTmsi.cpp, encode() - the function already returns bool
uint32_t tmsi = 0;
try {
    tmsi = (uint32_t) std::stoul(m_TmsiValue);
} catch (const std::exception&) {
    return false;
}
```

That covers both routes into the encoder. Separately, `ue_ngap_context::s_tmsi` should be populated where the
5GS TMSI is known, or the IE omitted when the context has none: returning `false` alone turns the crash into
messages that silently lose an IE they were meant to carry.

items.title: Complete the PDU Session Resource Modify Response handling: optional IEs and error propagation

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
## Summary

PR #3 (`feat(qos): relay network-initiated QoS modification to UE and RAN`) established the relay from the SMF to the UE and the RAN: `N1N2MessageTransfer` → `PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY REQUEST` + DL NAS. That direction is verified working.

To complete the procedure, the response from the NG-RAN (`PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY RESPONSE` → `Nsmf_PDUSession_UpdateSMContext`) needs two additions: **decoding support for the message's optional IEs**, and **error handling** so a QoS change the RAN could not apply is reported back to the SMF, the PCF and the AF. The two are linked — the failure information lives in one of those optional IEs — so they are best done together.

Line references are against `develop` @ `3bb4508b` and its pinned `src/common-src` @ `080ac1a6`.

---

## 1. Optional IEs are not implemented yet

`PduSessionResourceModifyResponseMsg` currently decodes only the two UE NGAP IDs and `PDUSessionResourceModifyListModRes`. All three optional IEs of the message are still open:

```
src/common-src/ngap/ngap_msgs/PduSessionResourceModifyResponse.hpp:38
  // TODO: PDUSessionResourceFailedToModifyListModRes (Optional)
  // TODO: User Location Information (Optional)
  // TODO: Criticality Diagnostics (Optional)
```

This is a prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have, for two reasons:

* `PDUSessionResourceFailedToModifyListModRes` is where the RAN reports which QoS flows it rejected and why. Without it there is no failure information to propagate at all.
* The decoder's `default:` branch returns `false` on any IE it does not recognise (`PduSessionResourceModifyResponse.cpp:247`), so a response carrying *any* of the three is rejected in full — including the PDU sessions the RAN did modify successfully. Making the branch skip-and-log, or implementing the IEs, is what allows real gNB responses through.

The asn1c types (`Ngap_PDUSessionResourceFailedToModifyListModRes` / `...ItemModRes`) are already generated, so this is C++ wrapper and wiring work. `PduSessionResourceFailedToSetupListSURes` is a good model to follow.

One related fix belongs here: `decode()` expects `Ngap_Criticality_reject` for the RAN UE NGAP ID IE (`PduSessionResourceModifyResponse.cpp:211`), while TS 38.413 §9.2.1.6 specifies `ignore`. OAI gNB sends `ignore` (`openair3/NGAP/ngap_gNB_pdu_session_management.c:206`), and the sibling decoders in `common-src` (setup, release, context modification) all check for `ignore` — this one is the outlier. Until it matches, no Modify Response decodes, so it is worth fixing first.

## 2. Error handling

The procedure currently has no path for reporting that something did not work. Four pieces are needed:

**Failure reporting to the SMF.** Once the failed list decodes, each failed item should go out as an `UpdateSmContext` with `n2SmInfoType = PDU_RES_MOD_FAIL`, mirroring the `PDU_RES_SETUP_FAIL` path that already exists for session setup (`src/ngap/ngap_message_callback.hpp:477`). Related: the handler returns early when the success list is absent (`ngap_message_callback.hpp:525`), but `PDUSessionResourceModifyListModRes` is optional — a response rejecting the only PDU session contains just the failed list, and that is the case that matters most.

**Malformed or undecodable responses.** When `decode()` fails, the AMF logs and drops. TS 38.413 expects an NGAP Error Indication so the gNB learns the message was not understood.

**No response at all.** `amf_n2::handle_itti_message(itti_pdu_session_resource_modify_request&)` (`src/amf-app/amf_n2.cpp:1302-1364`) sends over SCTP without a guard timer. If the gNB never answers, nothing expires and nothing is reported.

**Retracting the N1N2 transfer.** The AMF answers the SMF with `N1_N2_TRANSFER_INITIATED` and then has no way to correct that. `N1N2TransferFailureNotification` (TS 29.518 §5.2.2.3.1) is not implemented anywhere in the tree — `grep -ri "failurenotification" src/` returns nothing. This is the same mechanism the CM-IDLE / paging gap from #3 needs, so implementing it once covers both.

Scoping note: the SMF has the matching `PDU_RES_MOD_FAIL` case but the body is a stub (`oai-cn5g-smf/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp:2445`). A coordinated SMF change is needed for the rejection to become visible to the PCF and the AF.

## 3. Smaller items in the same procedure

* `UserLocationInformation` from the response is not forwarded, and `ueLocation` is absent from the `UpdateSmContext` body built in `src/amf-app/amf_sbi.cpp:485-517` (it is only set at session establishment, line 800). Useful for charging and location-dependent policy.
* The optional UE-AMBR IE is omitted from the Modify Request — `PduSessionResourceModifyRequestMsg` has no setter yet (`src/amf-app/amf_n2.cpp:1341`, TS 38.413 §9.3.1.47). Carried over from #3.
* RAN-initiated modification (`PDU SESSION RESOURCE MODIFY INDICATION` / `CONFIRM`, `ngap_message_callback.hpp:1017`) is still a stub. Separable follow-up — listed for completeness, not part of this issue.

## Proposed work items

**`oai-cn5g-common-src`**

1. Align the RAN UE NGAP ID criticality check with TS 38.413 §9.2.1.6 (`reject` → `ignore`).
2. Make the decoder's `default:` branch skip-and-log instead of failing the message; worth auditing the other `ngap_msgs/*.cpp` decoders for the same pattern.
3. Add `PduSessionResourceFailedToModifyItemModRes` / `...ListModRes` wrappers plus a getter on the response message.
4. Decode and expose `UserLocationInformation` and `CriticalityDiagnostics`.
5. Add a UE-AMBR setter to `PduSessionResourceModifyRequestMsg`.

**`oai-cn5g-amf`**

6. Forward failed items as `n2SmInfoType = PDU_RES_MOD_FAIL`, and stop returning early when the success list is absent.
7. Forward `UserLocationInformation` and populate `ueLocation` on `UpdateSmContext`.
8. Send an NGAP Error Indication when a response fails to decode.
9. Add a guard timer for the Modify Request and an `N1N2TransferFailureNotification` sender.
10. Set the UE-AMBR IE on the Modify Request once the setter exists.

**`oai-cn5g-smf`**

11. Implement the `PDU_RES_MOD_FAIL` case so the rejection reaches the PCF and the AF.

## Acceptance criteria

* A Modify Response carrying `UserLocationInformation` and/or `CriticalityDiagnostics` is decoded and processed.
* A response containing only `PDUSessionResourceFailedToModifyListModRes` produces an `UpdateSmContext` with `n2SmInfoType = PDU_RES_MOD_FAIL` and the unsuccessful transfer as `n2SmInfo`.
* A partially-successful response produces one `PDU_RES_MOD_RSP` per modified session and one `PDU_RES_MOD_FAIL` per failed session.
* An AF Quality-on-Demand request that the gNB rejects is reported as failed to the PCF and the AF.
* A Modify Request with no response from the gNB is reported upward rather than expiring silently.

## Notes

The findings above come from code review against `develop`, plus a cross-check of the OAI gNB encoder. The criticality mismatch in §1 blocks every Modify Response from decoding, so it masks the rest in any current deployment — fix it first, then re-run the AF Quality-on-Demand capture from #3 to observe the remaining behaviour.

The UE's `PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMPLETE` travels separately via `UL NAS Transport` and is not covered by this issue.

## Related

* AMF PR #3 (`feat-network-init-qos-mod`, merged as `1bd47873`)
* SMF: https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/pull/5 · PCF: https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-pcf/pull/2
* TS 38.413 §9.2.1.6 (Modify Response), §9.2.1.8 (Modify Indication), §9.3.1.47 (UE-AMBR)
* TS 29.502 §5.2.2.3 (`UpdateSMContext`, N2 SM information types)
* TS 29.518 §5.2.2.3.1 (`N1N2TransferFailureNotification`), §6.3.5
* TS 23.502 §4.3.3.2 (PDU Session Modification)
